checks.claim: HTTP 200 no longer conflates Applied and NoOp
checks.evidence: decode_replay requires boolean wakeApplied and then deserializes the matching result type; missing discriminator, wrong type or variant fields fail InternalConsistency.

checks.claim: Stored deterministic rejection remains an error with the same mapped status and code
checks.evidence: Explicit supported (status,error code) pairs reconstruct the five existing error variants. Unknown or mismatched pairs fail closed. InvalidCause preserves original detail from the hash-bound cause.

checks.claim: Cause reconstruction is bound to the original request
checks.evidence: Unchanged compute_wake_request_hash includes command schema/type, principal, exact instance/visit, expected version and Option<String> cause in the JCS envelope; acquire_receipt compares its hash before decode_replay. Relies on the normal application caller and hash integrity, not on arbitrary externally supplied storage hashes.

checks.claim: Receipt ownership, processing and command identity are retained
checks.evidence: Scope remains principal_id+idempotency_key under the existing unique constraint. Replay requires the Wake command type, matching hash and COMPLETED with status/body. PROCESSING is returned without taking ownership; other incomplete completion shapes fail InternalConsistency.

checks.claim: Replay does not re-evaluate fresh business state
checks.evidence: Receipt replay returns before actor/business-state/visit/CAS classification. Real-transition tests preserve previously stored NoOp and Applied outcomes after visit/version changes.

checks.claim: Deterministic rejection is durably completed before it is reported
checks.evidence: deterministic_failure consumes the actual owned transaction, completes the existing receipt, adds a non-sensitive WAKE_REJECTED code audit, awaits commit, then returns the original domain error. Every call site is before business success mutation.

checks.claim: Commit failure is not mislabeled as successful or known deterministic rejection
checks.evidence: All outcomes await commit with storage error propagation. New deferred-constraint test targets rejection and Applied paths and distinguishes known database rejection from lost commit acknowledgement.

checks.claim: Applied/NoOp audit and business cardinalities follow the affected contracts
checks.evidence: Applied adds WAKE_APPLIED in the same transaction as one eligibility event, one version increment, one business Event and one receipt. NoOp preserves business state while keeping its existing receipt and WAKE_NO_OP audit. Replays preserve the original owned-outcome records; conflicts use the existing conflict audit.

checks.claim: No new auth rule, public error taxonomy, schema or production operation is introduced
checks.evidence: HTTP scope/direct-token/scheduler-role checks, DTOs, request hashing, error mapping and migrations are unchanged. Audit labels fit existing free-text attempt_type constraints; rejection audits store code rather than cause payload.

checks.claim: Regressions exercise material boundaries rather than only mirroring a decoder
checks.evidence: Eight new PG/application/HTTP test functions cover natural ALREADY_DUE, mismatch/cancel/closed, state change replay, exact Applied effects, changed-hash conflict, durable rejections, disabled-actor original result, two concurrent-key patterns, and deferred commit rejection. Two unit tests cover malformed receipt schema/status/code.

unresolved_boundaries: No Rust/SQL whole-program formal refinement or production acceptance is claimed.

PrincipalNotFound has a supported decoder branch, but normal new receipt acquisition is constrained by the principal FK and HTTP gate; this is not a claimed successful PG fixture for a nonexistent actor.
VISIT_NOT_CURRENT is covered at codec level only. Normal transition fixtures close the source activation first and legitimately exercise ACTIVATION_CLOSED.
Storage errors remain the existing public infrastructure class; no new committed/rolled-back certainty is inferred from a lost acknowledgement.
Replay assumes integrity of completed receipt content and request hashing; full JSON/parser/cryptographic correctness is outside this source review.
Missing parent-authority acceptance and full-repository governance conformance remain separately unresolved; the patch does not silently restore recovered files.
